title: This review is for unboxing and setup review only
text:
Delivered 30 November 2023. Today is 06 January 2024. 

The unboxing and assembly instructions were very easy to follow and were spot-on.  Unfortunately, the chimney cap bolt was improperly machined (i.e., the bolt threads were not properly machined to match the threads of the pipe) which caused the chimney cap bolt to become cross-threaded as I was installing the bolt into the pipe.  The threads on the chimney pipe were undamaged.  I purchased an after-market chimney cap and chimney pipe, they were not sold separately, and I only used the nuts and bolts from the new cap to secure the original chimney cap to the original chimney pipe.  The after-market nuts and bolts were a perfect match for the original chimney cap and chimney pipe.

As of this review, 06 January 2024, I have not used the Traeger for grilling because I wanted to resolve the cross-threaded bolt issue.

title: Good grill not so good design
text:
We purchased the Traeger Timberline XL in September/October 2022. We loved the concept that it can be built into an outdoor kitchen with cabinets for a cleaner look. The smoker/grill is amazing and food is delicious however, the design of the Timberline XL is not so great. 
The Timberline XL design is different than all the other models in a sense that it has built in storage under the grill. When we got our grill and set it up, everything was great until a week later we had a major rain storm in the Florida keys and everything that was in the inside storage underneath the grill got wet. I contacted Traeger because I noticed that the magnet door closure started to rust and wanted to know how the water is getting in. I was basically told that I should have bought a cover for the grill. For the price of almost $4,000.00 you could just add the cover which costs $150 or specify that it needs a cover not listed under essentials accessories. We have owned a Traeger before and never used a cover rain or shine in the FL keys. We ended up buying one for the Timberline XL because we had no choice.  At this juncture, my cast iron pans and cutting boards went to the garbage, the probe attachment will eventually fail from getting wet and Traeger blew it off like we should know it needs a cover. Water will get into the probe hole if it's raining and eventually cause issues with that. Because of the design of the grill a cover is needed and I wished that at this price Traeger would just include it with the grill or charge the $200 more and include it. Leaving it as a option to buy is pointless because as customer service told me "its needed."
Additionally, the bamboo shelves are also pointless because with the grill being covered and no air circulation they are in the garbage because they were covered with mold from all the humidity and Florida weather. With or without cover the bamboo shelves are a failed feature because they will get mold from being covered or rained on. 
In conclusion besides a cleaner and nicer build in look, the design of the Timberline XL is not good at all and unless you are looking for a clean outdoor kitchen look I would buy the older freestanding models. This grill is too expensive to have these issues.

title: Best design and engineering of any pellet grill
text: I have owned several pellet grill brands. I have owned Yoder, Memphis, Recteq, Camp Chef and Pitts and Spitts. The engineering and design of the Traeger Ironwood XL surpasses all of them by a long shot. First of all the grease management system is the best I have seen as is the removeable fire pot for cleaning. I have never in all the bands I have owned had a pellet grill put out the amount of good smoke (thin blue smoke) this does even without the super smoke on. With the super smoke on it is out of this word with good smoke production. The controller is definitely the best in the business and the integrated app has options most don't have. The WIFI was very easy to set up and was working within 3 minutes. The lights that come on when the lid is opened are fantastic. Most brands have them in the interior of the grill and are worthless after 2 cooks. These lights are not to the lid on the exterior of the barrel and do not get covered in smoke. The grill when running is very quiet. I have had other brands where I am laying in bed and can hear the blower motor and auger running and were pretty loud. The pop and lock rail system is very awesome. I have bought the front shelf, Basket, drink holder and 2 roll holder/dispensers, One for paper towel and one for butcher paper. I have found the cooking surface to be very even with temp. I have cooked almost everything I always cook and everything has awesome bark and very good smoke flavor. I cooked a brisket overnight and it used about a half hopper of pellets. The lighted pellet hopper and pellet sensor tells the percentage of pellets left and has a low pellet alarm as well. Cleaning after cooking is a breeze, The porcelain grates are easy to clean with a hot cloth and wiped off. After a 12 hour cook very little ash. The fire grate comes out and you can vacuum out under it. I like the pellet auger drops the pellets down into the burn grate so you will never get back burn.

title: Beware. Not a long term product. Not worth the $
text:
My wife bought this grill for me 3 years ago for Father’s Day. I was very excited because I’d heard all the wonderful things about it. It was also a rather extravagant gift at nearly $1800 all in (prices have come down a bit).  First the good:  It is a superior product over most other grills.  It cooks evenly and the e wood pellets make anything you cook taste SO good!  The supersmole feature is an excellent touch as well but only if it’s a small project like a small ham or pork shoulder (for larger items such as Goose, Turkey, etc) I would still recommend a standalone smoker.  It’s Reasonably easy to operate and the app (when it works; more on that later) He is really terrific and helpful.

Now the bad news:  The app loses connection regularly And restoring it can often take quite a bit of time, which is pretty inconvenient when you’re trying to get something cooked. But that’s the least of the issues. The auger got jammed (Without us, realizing it, and without any alert on the app) Which backed up all of the pellets into the hopper box, which started a fire. We did not panic; we simply removed all the pellets shut down the grill And waited for everything to burn off which it did pretty quickly. We contacted customer service and we had to replace the control board and sensor which we did (about $500) and we took the motor off and cleared the auger manually as instructed. Ever since that time, the grill simply does not work. It takes forever to get started, and the auger still does not work properly. We reached out to support who suggested a few different companies in the area that could come out and service the grill. We chose one of those. ($100) After two weeks when they came out, they basically told us the grill was shot. They said, even if they could repair it, the cost would be more than that of a new Traeger. But, they wouldn’t repair it, because they couldn’t ensure that it would be safe after the fire.

So now, we have a (With all associated costs) a $2,000 platter box. We made one final call to customer service who said that there was really nothing they could do about it and that these things happen. And, I get it. Nothing lasts forever. As I said at the beginning, it’s a next level Product to begin with and when it works, it’s fantastic. But, it appears as though the shelflife of this is 3.5 years.  So, depending on your perspective and bank account, you lease the grill in effect, for $571 a year and then apparently throw it out?

Overall, we’re disappointed because we don’t have that kind of money. And, the amount of time we had to spend on this thing not to mention the money, which ultimately did not even yield into a useable Product was pretty frustrating. Customer service was very polite and kind, but, it’s clear that these things have a life expectancy. So, despite the fact, I do not prefer propane cooked grilled food, That’s what I’m back to.

This isn’t a post to tell you not to buy this unit, just to be aware of what you’re getting yourself into.

text:
So disappointed in this grill.  I've looked at in the store it for over a year and finally pulled the trigger and wish I hadn't.  Hardly got hot during the seasoning process, so cool that the oil didn't even dry or burn off.  Spent over 4 hours troubleshooting the inability to connect to wifi, going through every guide and video I could find for this controller (which are very difficult to find).  Waited on the phone for customer service for 55 min only to spend an hour walking through all of the stuff I had already done.  Customer service rep was nice but no help nor was the supervisor he was working with.   
Neither was able to tell me how to do a hard reset on the controller or how I can check/force a firmware update.  As a last resort I finally decided to pull apart my brand new grill to check the wifi antenna and, sure enough, it wasn't connected to the board.  
After repairing that I tried to fire it up to try a cook.  Set it for 350 and after 80 min it only reached 225 degrees so I gave up and put it to shutdown mode.   After cooking in my oven and eating, I restarted it and set it for 500 to see what would happen.  After an hour it just barely made it to 400, so I reset it at 400 to see if it would at least hold and.....nope.  Settled at 340 and came back up to 360 and hovered between there and 345.  Waited an hour on the phone again and gave up.  
After reading the reviews a bit closer on this thing I see this seems to be a common enough problem and they sure aren't making them like the last 2 Traegers I've owned. I'm not sticking around to shotgun troubleshoot and deal with this like others have.  It's going back to the store while the getting is good and I still can.
Sorry Traeger, you lost a lifelong customer.

title: Poor lid construction
text: I purchased my Pro 780 at the Houston Rodeo several years ago. I can say I enjoy it but it is a shame to me that it does not completely meet this statement found on their website:  "WILL THIS GRILL FALL APART WITHIN A YEAR? Traeger grills are built-to-last. Every Traeger features superior structural construction, an ultra-sturdy base, and built-tough steel legs. If something does go wrong, our ironclad 3-year warranty and 365 days of customer service will cover any issue that may arise." Honestly the only place it has superior struction is in the base of the pit but not where the pit is used the most which is the lid. Less than a year the the opening and closing of the lid weakened the lid hinges and screws. The hinges began to bend then tear due to not being able to handle the weight of the lid when opened. There is nothing off load the lid's wiehgt off the hinges. I looked at other pellet grills such as the Ptit Boss and saw how they structured their support for the lid when open. I wish Treagar had the same. Due to the hinges bending the door does not close correctly. I did call customer service. I had to go through a process I am sure they have done quite often with may other customers and of course it did not resolve the issue. They sent another lid, hinges and handle but in no time the same thing is happening. The hinges are bending due to the weight of the lid and lid not closing correctly. I guess I will have to call agian to get it all replaced. These pits are not cheap but it sould not be advertised as "superior structural construction" because the lid system is not superior at all.

title: It’s fine, but over priced.
text:
I’ll start by saying that there are some pros and cons to this smoker. Pros: Lot’s of cooking space, probably more than I needed for my family of three. Heavy duty grill grates, even the top racks are stainless steel and feel solid. You won’t see these in the less expensive models. It seems to cook evenly across the surface. Pellet bin is probably the easiest to clean out along with the drip bucket. It has a nice drip tray that cleans easily and I think the heat shield works as it should. The touchscreen for the controller is great, it’s easy to use and I love the induction burner. Also, the grill grates on the bottom are in three pieces and will fit in my dishwasher. The grill looks nice and the casters roll well. Assembly will take a few hours. It’s extremely heavy and you’ll need someone helping you put it together.
The cons. It’s expensive. The app won’t stay connected to the smoker as it should. After many phone calls to Traeger, they ultimately decided it’s my problem because my WiFi is overused. Who knew 1gig fiber optic is not compatible with their controller and app. The controller only works on 2G, so my router is separated between 2and 5G with the bulk of date is being used on the 5G. I’m now experiencing one of the wireless meat thermometer trying to connect to the controller while it’s in its charging base. I don’t know what’s going on with that, but I refuse to call in just to be connected to someone overseas. That’s right, Traeger outsources its call center. Traeger claims that all the ash from the burn pot is supposed to blow into the drip bucket, it does not. In fact, there is very little ash in there. I had to buy a small shop vac just to get it all out. The inside of the smoker has where the pot is and the drip bucket are separated by a large hill like piece of metal.
Overall, it cooks as it should. I wish the app would work like it’s supposed to and the ashes would make it into the drip bucket. I should have reviewed more high end smokers before purchasing to see what I was missing out on, but where I live, we only have big box stores. I think if you spend half of what this Timberline XL cost, you’ll be missing heavier grates, induction burner, 2 wireless thermometers and maybe a little square footage of cooking space.

title: Not what I expected for the price
text:
It started with the shipping process. About 4 days after I ordered my Traeger Timberline XL, it was still showing “order being processed” on their website. On the 5th day it showed shipped. I called to get an estimate of when it would arrive as I was preparing for a large party and was hoping to have it by then. 40 minutes later I finally got a live person on the phone. 
Even though the “agent” was very polite and kind, she could not tell me when it would arrive. I then asked her where it shipping from and she could not answer that. I asked her if there was a tracking number, and she said not at this time. I asked her if she knew where it was, and she said no and all she could tell is that it left the warehouse. I said, what warehouse and she said she didn’t know. So now I said, Traeger has shipped one of its grills, and has no idea where it went or where it left from?  She said, that is correct but it has been shipped and you should get it soon. She said she would follow up with a tracking number in an email the next day. I said ok and since I was getting anywhere I thanked her and hung up. In all, this took about 30 minutes on the phone with her because she kept putting me on hold to research my questions. 
The next day I texted the same question via there “online live support.”  I asked the support person to call me asap. When I finally got the call I started asking the same questions as the day before. This time they had a tracking number from AAA Cooper Transportation but once again had no idea where the grill was. I asked to speak to a manager and a very arrogant guy came on the line. I asked him, where is my grill and he said he wasn’t sure but he “thought” is was probably shipped from Auburn Wa warehouse which is about 20 minutes from my home. He couldn’t give any verification of where it was shipped from or where it was and his attitude was clearly an attitude of “and I don’t really care.”  I was done. I decided to call AAA Cooper Transportation myself who is located in Alabama. A lady came on the line and I gave her the tracking number. She said she thinks it might be at a warehouse in SeaTac Wa and she gave me their number. I called them and they said it was given to another shipping company and is probably in Tacoma Wa and she gave me their number. I called them and immediately the lady recognized my name and said “Oh, we have your shipment.”  I said great, when will
It be delivered?  She said, next week. I asked, can I pick it up? She said, come on down, we’ll help you load it. So 7 days after I ordered it, which had started out in a warehouse 20 minutes from my home, I had to drive an hour to pick it up so I could have it in time for my party. 
You will likely read that Traeger customer support is for the most part worthless and time consuming. I  here to attest in full that that is very true. 
My grill, once I put it together, does not hold a consistent temp. 2 days ago I spent and hour and a half on an “online chat support” asking why my Traeger which I had set to 250 degrees, would get to that temp and then go back down to 203 before starting to come back up to 250 and then passing 250 for 282. The answer was, a fluctuation of 25 degrees is normal. I said, “you can’t do math very well as my is fluctuating -47 degrees and some times +32.”  
I’ve given up on Traeger. Poor customer service, poor support, and an overly priced product that doesn’t do what they say it will do. I’m not even going to go into the fact that my upper grills do not fit correctly and won’t stay in place. I think the grill is bowed outward at the top. 
It’s unfortunate that I’m going to recommend you go with another brand. For the last 5 years I’ve used another brand and never had any issues. I finally wore out the smoker I had been using so I thought I would upgrade to the Mac daddy Timberline XL and instead it turned out to be an expensive downgrade.

If you use a cover, the pail  falls when you remove the cover. I needed to design a latch that retains the pail. It could been designed a lot better without adding cost.  Hopper clean out is difficult as the door is behind the grill and the pellets do not free flow out of the hopper. A stick needs to be poked through the anger protection screen.  I'm sure that many people have just removed the screen.  The controller is easy to operate and the Mobil app screen is laid out well.  Cleaning the ash put requires all the heat shields and grates to be removed. Chamber cannot be removed and dumped, it has to be vacuumed.  Other competing grill have buckets that can be removed.  All in all, heat stability is good, controller is good but the pellet unloading process and ash pit cleaning ergonomics could be a lot better.  It a middle of the rode product at best.

title: Minimal to no smoke.
text:
The good: maintains stable temp

The bad: little to no smoke flavor. Only able to use super smoke <225 even at that minimal smoke flavor. 

First cook:  18lb brisket, very tender and juicy. 885 regulated the temp very well. Confirmed internal temp with electric oven thermometer and an analog oven therm. But it had almost zerrrro smoke flavor. 

2nd cook: 4 racks baby back. Added smoke tube and ran first hour at 225 super smoke. Better smoke flavor but still not enough for spending 1300$ traeger.

title: Caster Wheels Fall Off
text:
bought the grill about a month ago. I assembled the grill and started rolling it into my garage. The surface of my driveway cement has a slight rough spot where the surface of the driveway has chipped away. When I wheeled it across that spot, the two caster wheels fell off. The wheels come attached to the legs so I know it wasn’t an assembly error. I contacted Traeger and the support agent was friendly and was very helpful…kind of. 

She was happy to send me a new set of wheels. I told the person that I was pretty sure the problem was with the way the wheels connected to the legs and as the wheels came attached to the legs, I think I need new legs not just the wheels. The agent was positive that the new wheels would solve the problem and sent me the new wheels. I recite new wheels and attached them to the legs. I moved the wheels carefully back and forth mimicking what had happened previously. I could easily pull the wheels off. 

So I called Traeger again. New agent, but just as friendly as the first. This agent had me take a short video showing how the wheels would easily come out of the legs. He agreed the problem was with the legs and offered to send me two new legs and some free rub for the inconvenience. New legs arrived today (no free rub…so much for my inconvenience) and I moved the wheel slightly back and forth as I had done previously, and the caster wheel came off. At this point I’m inclined to think there might be a design problem. The smoker legs showed up today. 

However, one has the same problem as the others. It is a design flaw. There’s a small ring around the peg of the caster wheel that slips into a very small grove in the leg’s sleeve. If the wheel is moved back and forth enough, the wheel easily slips out of the grove and falls off. 

The problem will occur if the wheels are on rough ground and catch on something while you’re pushing it. The force of trying to push the grill over the catch is enough to cause that small ring to slip out of the groove resulting in the wheel coming off. I’m still excited to use the smoker. I just need to remember that pushing the smoker over any rough spot in the cement may cause the wheels to fall off. This is my fourth smoker. My last smoker was the Ironwood 885. Never a problem. It wheeled over the same rough spot without difficulty. Part of me thinks that maybe I was better off sticking with that smoker.

title: If you enjoy headaches, this thing is for you!
text:
I’ve been using my Timberline 1300 for a few years now. It’s a decent smoker and does its job well when it works. If you’re thinking about grilling on this thing though, go somewhere else. If you live in a colder climate and want to grill year round, this grill is not for you. 

This grill is also not for you if you’re on a time crunch. The grill takes absolutely forever to get up to temp (if it actually even makes it to the temp you set it to). Then, good luck holding that temp once you put in your meat. They’ll blame it on poor quality pellets, even when you’re using a fresh bag of their own. 

If you’re lucky enough to get to a high temp, then you get to see how easy it is to start a grease fire in the thing. The fire usually likes to then work its way down the auger, burning up all the pellets along the way, so be ready to empty your hopper so they all don’t go up in flames. 

With the high temps then comes peeling paint and inevitable rust! Fun! Even if you keep it covered religiously when it’s not in use, you won’t escape this either. 

I hope Traeger is embarrassed charging as much as it does for this grill, because I’m sure embarrassed that I purchased one.

I'd recommend a hand truck to move it to where you're going to build it.  

The packaging that was used was incredibly well done and would make it fairly difficult, but not impossible, to damage in transit.  The only drawback to that was that there was a literal mountain of cardboard that needed to be dealt with, but no regrets...

The main reason I liked the idea of the app controlled grill/smoker was with the intention that I could fire up the grill and let it come to temp just by using my app while prepping food in my kitchen. If I have to go out to start the grill I am setting the temp at that time also so what is the point. Long story short the App is pointless bordering on false advertising. 
Lastly, it takes half an hour to heat up to grilling temperature. This would be made more tolerable if I could start it remotely but as mentioned above, that isn't possible. title: 'Underwhelmed' is probably the best description
text:
I have owned my Ironwood 885 for almost 3 years. It is operating as designed with no major issues that many other reviews have mentioned. There have never been any network issues or structural/finish issues (no paint flaking, etc.), and for the most part, no operational issues. I'm just overall underwhelmed with its performance now that I have had opportunities to compare it to other pellet grills of the similar design. (no, I'm not comparing a pellet grill with a true 'stick burner/offset')

I've cooked with true wood burning/smoking prior to getting the Ironwood. The taste and flavour can't really be matched (nor did I expect it to be), however I wanted the ease and automated control of a programmable pellet grill, and “meet in the middle” for 'wood-fired'. This is where it under performs. As far as the technology and automatic control goes, it does the job. However, there is very little actual 'wood-fried’ flavour and I have now spent a few years trying different temperatures, different pellet fuel (yes Traeger brand pellets as well), "super-smoke" mode (which makes little to no difference), and varying timeframes to no avail. Sure, I can add an aftermarket 'smoke tube' to burn in the chamber to add smoke flavour, but doesn't that defeat the purpose of a pellet grill/smoker?? It now becomes an expensive outdoor oven with a smoke tube. This is where I’m at however, and, shouldn’t be the case.

Lastly, the temperature sensor/control of the cooking chamber has never been accurate, on average running about 20C lower than the display reads. There is a calibration for the temperature probes, but none for the built-in sensor. Using numerous secondary thermometers (INLCUDING a Meater Probe owned by Traeger themselves) The temperature on those thermometers is 20C lower than then Ironwood says. Hence, you must set and run the Ironwood at approx. 20C higher to get the chamber temperature you desire. This is especially problematic if you want to run at 225C (the maximum temp Super Smoke will work) but have to set it at 245C in order to get real-world 225C. Setting it at 245C disables Super Smoke, while on the other end, if you set it at 225C the real-world temp is about 200C, resulting in increasing cooking times significantly. So yes, while it is functional, it's problematic, and after researching online there is no known fix (it’s long out of warranty but has been a consistent problem since day one.) 

All in all, I enjoy the look, build, and finish of the unit. It's well-built, just quite underwhelming in performance when compared to the same cooks side-by-side with a close competitor, Reqtec. For the high price, I would say it’s below-average, and would not buy Traeger again. Evaluated against a friend's dozens and dozens of cooks over the same time period, side by side on his Reqtec 700, if I had to do it again I would buy a Reqtec which is of similar build quality, wifi technology, achieves closer to a true wood fired smoker and, with accurate temps. Unfortunately, I'm not going to recoup the money spent in reselling the Ironwood, in order for me to switch at this point.

title: A $3,300 Headache Right Out of the Box
text:
Today I had the misfortune of experiencing a disastrous unboxing and assembly process with my new Traeger Timberline grill. The assembly process took about 90 minutes (pretty straight forward), but when I finally plugged it in, the unit was dead on arrival—the display didn't turn on at all. This was incredibly disappointing given that it's a brand-new purchase.

To resolve the issue, I spent another 90 minutes waiting on hold for a Traeger Support technician.  Once connected, we spent another hour troubleshooting the issue together. This process was somewhat tedious, as it involved disconnecting numerous small connectors from the controller board and wire harness. Unfortunately, the call concluded with them deciding to send me a new hopper assembly containing all the electronics.

While I understand that parts may take some time to arrive—about a week in this case—I'm deeply frustrated by being expected to perform what they describe as "self-repair." This is not what I anticipated when spending over $3,000 on this product. Although shipping and parts are covered under warranty, it feels like resolving this issue has become my responsibility rather than theirs.

Overall, my experience has been marred with disappointment and frustration, not only with the product's poor performance straight out of the box but also with the prospect of spending additional time replacing parts. I foresee wasting hours on a Saturday dealing with these issues, which is far from what I expected when purchasing this product.

title: Great value for the money!
text:

The auger/fan assembly was moved to underneath the main body, held on by 4 bolts. This is a much improved design if you need to access those parts for repair. The grease trap being moved to underneath now keeps me from knock8ng the fan off every time I take the cover off. The features added on the controller are very nice for the price point. This is a lot of grill for $1,000 and improved in most areas over the older pro and ironwood models I've previously owned.

title: Let Down After Years of Loyalty. Safety Concerns
text:
I’ve been a huge Traeger fan and loved my grill for years — until recently, when it became unsafe to use. After following guided instructions from Traeger customer service on a video call, my grill caught fire so badly that the interior and lid began melting rapidly and ended up chipping apart on the inside. That’s a serious health and safety concern for my family.

I was told the issue stemmed from rust in the fire pot, which supposedly created a fire hazard — but that wasn't the original issue I called about. Now I have a $1,300 grill that’s unsafe to cook on, despite regular maintenance and care. I was told to replace the firepot even though it's flaking inside the lid when I would have never let a massive fire "go out on it's own".  Their offer? A 15% discount on a new one.

I expected more from a brand that claims their grills are “built to last” and that they “stand by their craftsmanship.” I followed their advice, and my grill is now toast — literally. Very disappointed in how this was handled. I’m hoping they make it right, but so far, the response has left me questioning my loyalty to Traeger.

text:
We love the grill but after using for a month or so, we do have a few things that annoy us. First are the wheels. They suck. WORST WHEELS EVER!!! The front wheels are caster and they pop off very easily. I did not realize they pop in and out and thought they broke. To get it back on you will need 2 people. One to lift the grill and the other will need to push (not twist) it back on. Very bad design. The rear wheels are fixed and not casters so it is nearly impossible to move the grill. All 4 should be on casters so you can easily move the grill. This is the worst part about the grill and it biggest design flaw and wish the rear legs had caster. 

The top adjustable shelf is problematic. If your cooking something larger like a whole chicken you will need to remove the top shelf so it will fit. We love the super smoke. This grill replaced our smaller Traeger (CostCo Silverton) that we had for 6 years and this is a big step up. This grill does use A LOT more pellets but then it is almost twice the size of our last grill. Occasionally we do have an issue with the grill not turning on. You push  the power button and nothing happens. Not sure why but if I turn if off and back on it usually comes on. It does run a bit hot. If I set the temp to 400 it seems to keep it at 425 according to the display. Our old one ran cooler. I was concerned about the ease of cleaning this one, but I have to admit it is easier to clean than our old one. It would be nice if they made a liner for the grill for even easier clean up.

title: A price vs. customer service mismatch…
text:
Traeger
I desperately wanted to love my Traeger Timberline, but it’s been an infuriating letdown. This $3,300 grill, hyped as a premium outdoor cooking masterpiece, has been a glorified lawn ornament for nearly a month due to a defective igniter. The first replacement igniter Traeger sent was also dead on arrival, doubling my frustration. A second replacement was promised before the weekend to salvage my plans, but Traeger’s hollow promises fell through—both parts are now expected after a maddening 10-day wait, with no option for expedited shipping.
Beyond my experience, other Timberline owners report a litany of issues that make this grill’s premium price tag feel like a cruel joke. Many complain of wildly inaccurate temperature controls, with some grills running over 100 degrees off the set point, rendering precise cooking impossible. Wireless meat probes frequently malfunction or fail to connect, leaving users to rely on third-party thermometers. Grease management is another sore point—poor drainage design leads to dangerous grease fires, with some users reporting flames shooting up the auger into the pellet hopper. WiFi connectivity, a touted feature, is notoriously unreliable, with the Traeger app often failing to sync or dropping connections mid-cook. Worst of all, Traeger’s customer service is consistently described as unresponsive, forcing owners to troubleshoot complex repairs themselves or wait weeks for parts, if they’re addressed at all.
My grill hasn’t been functional long enough to encounter these additional headaches, but given Traeger’s track record, I’m bracing for more disappointment. For a grill priced like a luxury car, I expected flawless performance and top-notch support. Instead, Traeger delivers a product that fails within 30 days and a customer service experience reminiscent of a shady used-car lot. This isn’t just a shame—it’s an outright betrayal of trust. Save your money and invest in a grill that doesn’t require constant babysitting or an engineering degree to fix.

title: Nice looking boat anchor
text:
I bought this during cowboy Christmas, in las vegas 2024. I received the grill very quickly. I was super excited, and was even impressed with the boxing of the grill. My kids had a blast with it... that's where the fun really stopped. 

Within the first week of using it, the cook top failed, turning on and off... BTW, it only really heats the center 5.5" of the pan. I bought the special traeger cast iron hoping it would disburse the heat more evenly, it doesn't. Even with the replacement cook top, it's only the 5.5" center that really reaches the temps claimed of 700°. I've tried several brands of cast iron and high carbon steel, all rated for induction tops with the same results. I guess it's cool for a sauce pan. 

As a low temp smoker, it's doing that fairly well. As a grill? Not so much. The constant high heat shut down, even when running it 475° like they recommend, it's terrible! I bought thier sear plates, will run the grill at 475° and still, if I close the lid and run inside, boom, over temp and cook takes forever to restart. I sure do miss my $700.00 pit boss I gave to my neighbor, before I even unboxed this grill. 

I never had any issues with it. I cooked everything with it, low and slow, high heat, never a problem. I was looking for something bigger and newer. I cook 90% of my meals on the grill, all year long here in vegas. I regret this purchase so much! I never do anything for myself and it was supposed to be something nice for me to cook my kids meals on. It's been more problems than it's worth. I should have either went with another pit boss, or a rec-tec, rated for higher temps. 

Save yourself the headache, and heartbreak... buy something else.

title: The Timberline XL is amazing
text: Amazing machine. Large capacity with ease of use. The smoke rings it generated were impressive. Set up and assembly instructions were easy to follow. The best feature is the conduction cooktop. To reverse sear with my Timberline 850, I had to put in the in searing plates, crank up the temp to 500 degrees and wait. This added almost an hour to my cooks. Now with my conduction cooktop and a ribbed cast iron skillet, I can sear the steaks as they reach internal temp. Cleaning the XL is still a chore. The disadvantage of such a large cook space. But it is easier overall than my 850. Handling pellets is much easier. Just put the container under the hopper and it empties directly in. My only criticism is the included Meater Wireless Thermometers. I’ve used Meater Thermometers for a long time and using them only to monitor internal temperature sells them short. The app that comes with Meaters is robust and useful and the included thermometers don’t sync with the Meater app. They only monitor internal temp on the XL.

title: Many Good Features
text:
My wife bought this for me on Father's Day, and I couldn't be happier. She bought it from Ace Hardware in Everett, WA where we live and they gave us free assembly and delivery. It works as advertised if one follows directions -- especially clean after each use. The grill is large enough to accommodate a large turkey as was my inaugural fare to smoke, plus some. I have read about the instability of temperature but haven't experienced that at all. It cooks evenly and the volume of smoke is more than sufficient to give meat its due smoky flavor.

The construction is solid, and the weight of the smoker affirms that, the lid is smooth shuts well. The interior   section fit and finish is nice -- the parts go in and out smoothly. The most important topic regarding construction is the linchpin/bushing auger assembly. As I have seen in a few videos, many auger failures mentioned in reviews may be a result of the unintentional removal of the linchpin eiher by jostling during assembly (inverting the barrel) or moving the smoker in a bumpy area. I believe that, according to videos, that the apparently undersized linchpin should be replaced with a properly sized bolt running through the bushing and the auger post, fastened with a lock washer would not only remedy the issue, but greatly reduce complaints about this issue.

title: Full of regret, 4th of July ruined.
text:
Bought the Pro Series 34 yesterday and seasoned per the instructions. Started it up early this morning and began smoking a Boston butt at 4am, at 250°F.  Everything was fine for several hours, until the igniter stopped working. Unfortunately I didn't notice it right away, and temperature in the cooking chamber dropped to 143°F before in realized what happened. This of course was frustrating, but I removed everything from inside the grill, cleared the fire pot of pellets and restarted the grill. Everything seemed fine, but after a while I noticed it was taking too long for the meat temperature to come up to where it should be. After 12 hours of cook time at 250°F, the meat probe was barely reaching 170°F. I've never had a butt take that long to cook. I checked it with my own thermometer and found it was actually 20° lower than the Traeger probe was indicating.  I then laid that probe on the cooking grate and closed the lid. The cooking chamber temperature as indicated on the meat probe was 20° lower than the temperature shown on the probe used for the controller. That's a total of 40° difference. I had to move the meat into my oven to finish it off.  I am now 14 hours in and just crossed over 180° as I type this.  My 4th of July celebration has been completely ruined thanks to this. This grill was the biggest waste of money, and that's saying something because I've given money to that Nigerian prince before.  

I will be returning this grill to Home Depot tomorrow and buying something else, from a different company.

title: Owning a new Woodridge Pro and a Weber Genesis
text: I purchased a Traeger Woodridge Pro about 3 months ago and its my first Smoker/Pellet Grill. I have been using a Weber Genesis for years and usually only cook for my wife and I but maybe 4 times per year I will cook for a family of 4 in addition to us. Capacity wasn't an issue, Construction is mostly good however I do wish the bottom plate that connects all 4 legs didn't seem like it would end up being the first part to begin to rust away because so much water collects on it anytime it rains. I purchased a Traeger Woodridge Pro OEM cover for it and while it is high quality I definitely concerned about the water collecting on the flat spots where the shelf and pellet bin are. As for Cooking, the wifi is great, I definitley love that and it cooked the best chicken I've had. It's ignition process was a little less intuitive than I had hoped but after I read the owners manual I was able to get the hang of it. As for Temperature.... It takes a while to get up to temperature especially when its raining/windy but holds it well until you open it for 20 seconds or more, then it takes a while to get back up again so its' a vicious cycle unless you set it and forget it to let the app and meat probes handle it all. I like not accidentally burning the meat like I had done on my Weber a few times but the chicken sometimes had a tough rubbery skin when I smoked it for too long or when the grill lid was open too long and the grill went all the way down to 95 degrees and took 20 minutes to get back up to temperature. Overall I'm happy with the purchase but I'll hang on to my Weber grill also so I can cook stuff hot and quick every now and again.

title: Unfortunate avoidable design shortfalls.
text:
LOVED this grill when I first got it a couple of years ago.  Still love the flavor of the food (when you use quality pellets), but there are some disappointing shortfalls.  

1)  I couldn't believe a $1,000 grill wouldn't come with a shelf already.  Had to purchase on separately for $80. 

2)  The lid is thin and, for some inexplicable reason, Traeger didn't see fit to reinforce where the lid restrictor is attached to the lid and the grill, inevitability leading to the lid bending enough over time that you don't get a tight fit when the lid's closed.

3) Seems like other manufacturers figured out that it's a good idea to sell heat resistant gaskets and lid locking devices to rectify this.  Although I was able to purchase an Oklahoma Joe's brand gasket at Lowe's, the lid still is not tight.  Oklahoma Joe's, LavaLock and others sell a lid latch kit for smokers, but, unfortunately, they don't seem to be compatible with he Traeger Pro 780 due too the narrow distance on the sides of the lid.

What i thought was a great pellet grill when I purchased it, turned out to be an overpriced average one.  Will definitely consider another brand when I upgrade.

title: The perfect entry into smoking for a beginner!
text:
I have wanted to get into smoking meat for a long time but was always intimidated by the process. I did not want to babysit a fire all night or constantly fiddle with vents. I finally decided to buy the Traeger Ironwood 650 as my very first smoker, and honestly, it makes me look like a professional pitmaster right out of the gate.

If you are a beginner like me and want to know if this investment is worth it, here is my breakdown of the experience.
Construction and Build Quality

Since this was my first unit, I was not sure what to expect regarding assembly and sturdiness. The Ironwood 650 is built like a tank. The legs are thick and stable, and the lid feels heavy and substantial when you open and close it.

The standout feature here is the double side wall insulation. I read that cheaper models leak heat, but this one holds temperature incredibly well. The gasket seals tight, so smoke actually stays inside the chamber where it belongs rather than leaking out the sides. It feels like a high end appliance rather than just a backyard grill.
Temperature Control

This was my biggest worry as a newbie. I had no idea how to manage airflow or fuel. The Ironwood 650 takes all that stress away with the D2 Direct Drive drivetrain. You literally just turn the dial to your desired temperature and hit ignite.

I watched the temperature on the digital display, and it is rock solid. If I set it to 225 degrees, it climbs there quickly and stays there. It recovers heat almost instantly after I open the lid to spritz the meat. It gives me total confidence that I am not going to ruin an expensive cut of meat by letting the heat spike or drop.
Cooking and Flavor

The flavor profile is amazing. I was worried that a pellet grill might not give enough smoke flavor compared to traditional offsets, but the Super Smoke mode solves that. You can toggle this feature on when cooking between 165 and 225 degrees. It forces more smoke over the meat without raising the heat.

My first cook was a brisket, and the results were shocking. It had a beautiful pink smoke ring and a distinct wood fired taste. The meat remained moist and tender. The convection fan circulates the heat and smoke evenly, so I did not even have to rotate the meat during the cook.
Capacity

Do not let the 650 number fool you. This size is perfect for a standard family. I have plenty of room for a full packer brisket and a pork butt at the same time. The grill comes with two porcelain coated racks. The bottom rack is adjustable, which is a great feature. I can lower it to fit a tall turkey or beer can chicken, or keep it higher for steaks and burgers. It strikes the perfect balance of being large enough for a party but not so massive that it takes up my whole patio.

There are two features that saved me during my first few cooks.

1) WiFIRE Technology: Being able to connect the grill to my phone via the Traeger app is incredible. I can sit on my couch and monitor the internal temperature of the meat and the grill temp. I can even change the temperature or turn on Super Smoke from my phone. It makes the long cooks very manageable.

2) Pellet Sensor: As a beginner, I have no idea how fast pellets burn. The built in sensor alerts my phone when the hopper is getting low. This saved me from running out of fuel during an overnight cook.

Conclusion

I am so glad I chose the Ironwood 650 as my first smoker. It removes the learning curve and lets you focus on prepping the food and enjoying the results. The construction is solid, the temperature is precise, and the food tastes incredible. I am officially hooked on smoking.

title: Grill fluctuates 45°; poor customer service.
text:
I’d like to preface this review with a little background on our experience with Traeger grills. We've had a Traeger Timberline 850 for 7 years, and we loved it so much that we bought two additional grills for our children. As our family grew, we needed more grilling space than the Timberline 850 could provide, so this past winter, we replaced it with the new Timberline XL.

Unfortunately, this new grill has been unable to maintain a consistent grilling temperature. The temperature fluctuates between 45–50°F, swinging from too hot to too cold. On one occasion, it even shut down due to excessive heat. I called customer service, and after a two-hour call, they determined we had a faulty thermocouple. They sent us a replacement, but the issue persisted, prompting another call.

During this second call, customer service determined that we needed an entirely new hopper assembly. The new hopper arrived and was installed, but the problem remained.

At this point, I had spent many hours on the phone and replaced several parts. Keep in mind, this grill cost us $4,000. I called customer service again to inquire about an exchange. This call lasted the entire afternoon. I went through the troubleshooting steps again, but because I was inquiring about an exchange this time I was told that the 45-degree fluctuations were within the normal range for this model. The tone of the conversation shifted after I asked about an exchange. I was also told that there had been a mistake in diagnosing the problem earlier, which led to the incorrect parts being sent.

However, during this call, they sent me a link to their official document that states, “Your grill should fluctuate no more than ±25 degrees”, which directly contradicted what I was being told.

I then asked to speak with the manager of the representative I’d been speaking with. When I spoke to him, I was again told that a 45-degree fluctuation was normal for this model. When I asked where this was documented, he admitted that it wasn’t. The next person I spoke with was his manager, who told me that the previous information was incorrect, that the fluctuations I was experiencing were due to an “overshoot,” and that I should never open the grill during a cook. I know that an overshoot doesn’t cause a constant 45-degree fluctuation above and below the set temperature for the entire duration of a cook.

Throughout this entire call, which stretched from afternoon into evening, I was given multiple excuses for why I was experiencing this issue. By the end, I felt like I was dealing with scammers, and this whole support experience has significantly diminished my perception of the Traeger brand.

Had I not previously owned a Traeger grill and been familiar with the brand’s quality, I would have been attempting a return instead of requesting an exchange

title: Whatever You Do - Don't Buy the Timberline XL
text:
I purchased my Timberline XL in December, 2025 at a local ACE store in Raleigh, NC.  After going through the initial burn-in, I started using the grill.  Immediately, I knew had a problem with the first-cook.  After 12 additional cooks, replacement of the thermostat, and multiple calls into Traeger Customer Service, the grill continues to have a number of problems.  

First and foremost, the cook chamber is not getting to temperature.  After having a 1300 for nearly a decade, I have done hundreds of pork shoulders and know when I am having a problem with my smoker. I bought the XL based on my complete satisfaction with the 1300.  That was a mistake.

The response from Traeger has been crickets.  After talking with customer service, the response was basically "you're screwed" we aren't going to replace the grill -- good luck.  The ACE dealer doesn't have any recourse either.  

It's disappointing when you have a company with a CEO who says he joined Traeger because of their commitment to the customer and the company basically says you're screwed and  "good luck with that one."

Furthermore, when they have paid endorsers like Heath Riles and Malcolm Reed, it damages their brand and trust levels too.  Another reason I went with the grill because I saw it being promoted by the leaders in outdoor barbecue, including Meat Church.

If you're looking at the Traeger Timberline XL grill - stop right now.  Proceed with caution, this is going to set you back $4000.00 and then you get a sub-par grill without any type of customer support and resolution.  

Traeger knows they are having problems with this unit, and they prefer not to address those concerns.  That's a big problem in my mind.

text:
I BBQ part-time professionally, primarily using larger wood and charcoal smokers.  Historically, I haven't really had much interest in pellet smokers. Not for any reason other than I simply enjoy the process of tending fires. I am, however, quite surprised, and not even a little embarrassed to admit how much I enjoy using my Traeger Woodridge Pro. In addition to the obvious convenience advantage compared to woodburning cookers, there is a great deal more to like about it... 

The controls are straightforward and very easy to use. The large, retro "8-bit"-style display is easy to see, even from a distance. The app is super intuitive and cleanly designed, without a lot of fluff or clutter between you and getting cooking. I appreciate that it uses Wi-Fi (rather than the more common Bluetooth), as Wi-Fi enables you to view and control a cook from anywhere you have cellular or Wi-Fi service! YES, I have indeed managed a cook, from a vehicle (as a passenger, of course), about 90 miles from home! The temperatures across the cook chamber, and top to bottom, are within reasonable differences. And the built-in food probe seems accurate when compared with my various 3rd-party leave-in thermometers.

Initially, I found the remaining pellet warning (a feature not included on the base model Woodridge) a little annoying. But I have to be honest, it's saved my “bacon” (almost literally) more than once! I got the alert when I was away from home toward the end of a long cook. And I was able to call a neighbor to come over and fill up the hopper!

While it may seem like a small thing to get excited about, it’s without doubt, THE easiest-to-clean pellet smoker I've ever used. Almost to the point of being enjoyable. There are hooks on the cooker body and framework where you can hang all the grates, including the primary drip tray, while you clean the inside. And unlike most other pellet smokers, there are no dark, hard-to-reach places inside. Once you remove the firepot cover, grease channel, and ash/grease keg cover (which all simply lift out with no contortions or gyrations required!), everything can be easily scraped or swept into the catch keg, then removed and dumped. Reading this as I'm writing it, it doesn't sound that easy. BUT TRUST ME, it really is incredibly easy. 

With all of these advantages, the REAL STANDOUT feature of the Woodridge for me is the way it cooks. Most horizontal, or what I call “offset style” (meaning a horizontal, barrel-style cook chamber with a pellet hopper to the side) pellet smokers have a tremendous issue with radiant heat, and cook more like an oven than a smoker, resulting in what I consider a less-than-optimal texture to your cooked food - ESPECIALLY BRISKETS, where I find the output from most pellet smokers to be noticeably "pot-roasty." 

What I'm assuming is happening with the Woodridge is that with the lighter weight and steeper angle of the primary drip tray, it's cooking more with convected (like a traditional offset smoker) than radiant heat. Whatever the actual contribution, the briskets I'm getting from my Woodridge are closer to traditional offset quality than I've ever had from a pellet smoker.

As far as anything negative to say. If you're planning to use this as much (or more) for grilling than smoking, this may not be the best choice for you. Not having any function for direct firepot access, you're limited to a max cook temp of about 500ºF. So you're not going to get that dark char that people are typically after. Not that you can't cook a decent steak or burger on it, but if I were looking to grill more than smoke, I'd probably be looking at another cooker.

Now I'm not ready to replace all my live-fire cookers with pellet smokers. But I did use it on customers' turkey cooks this holiday season (all of which turned out great!). And on the days I don't have the time, energy, or inclination to tend a fire, and just want some great food, the Woodridge has changed my thinking about pellet smokers, and has certainly earned its place in my lineup.

title: Timberline 1300 4 Year review
text:
I purchased my Timberline 1300 four years ago, and overall it has been an excellent grill.

Pros:
It delivers outstanding results with beef, chicken, and turkey, and it truly takes much of the guesswork out of cooking. The build quality is impressive — the grill feels extremely sturdy and well-made. Despite its weight, it is surprisingly easy to move around. Most importantly, the cooking performance has been consistently excellent.

Cons:
After approximately 1.5 to 2 years, rust began developing on the wheels, the bottom edge of the lid, and the rear smoke plate became heavily rusted as well.

Another concern, however, is the app and Wi-Fi connectivity. While the app has great potential, it frequently loses connection to my phone and often requires reconnecting to the Wi-Fi network. I have a strong wireless mesh setup with 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz coverage, with reliable signal even across the street, so network strength is not the issue. Because of the repeated connectivity problems, I eventually stopped using the app altogether.

That said, I have no complaints about the grill’s actual cooking performance — it truly is fantastic. However, the app reliability, Wi-Fi connectivity, and rust issues definitely need to be addressed.

title: Survived a 75mph tumble off my truck, still cooks
text:
I’ve had this Traeger since July 2020, and it just proved its durability in the most unexpected way. While moving, it came loose in my truck bed and got knocked out by a crosswind gust passing through a mountain pass, while I was doing 75 mph on the highway. I pulled over, gathered the pieces off the shoulder, hauled it home, and put it back together.

Damage was honestly minor considering what it went through: the cover got torn up, there are scratches down the back, and the smokestack bolt got ground flat at an angle from sliding on the pavement. That’s it. No cracks in the body, nothing structural. I hooked it back up, it fired up like nothing happened, and I’ve been cooking on it regularly ever since. If a grill can survive sliding down a highway at 75 mph and keep working perfectly, that tells you everything about the build quality. I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend Traeger to anyone shopping for a pellet grill, these things are built like tanks.

It consistently fails to meet reasonable expectations, and I have spent a significant amount of time trying to troubleshoot an issue that clearly impacts its performance.

Offering me a 25% discount on the purchase of another Traeger is not an acceptable resolution. After this experience, I have no confidence in purchasing another one of their products.

What is most disappointing is that Traeger has chosen not to stand behind its product. I purchased this grill because of the company's reputation for quality and customer service, and this experience has completely changed my opinion of the brand.

I have recommended Traeger to many people over the years, but I will no longer be doing so. In fact, I don't even feel comfortable selling my current grill second-hand because I don't believe it performs as it should, and I wouldn't feel right passing that problem on to someone else.

This outcome has left me incredibly disappointed and disheartened. As a result, I no longer consider myself a Traeger customer, and I have no intention of purchasing another Traeger product in the future.

I had hoped for a resolution that reflected confidence in your products and commitment to your customers. Unfortunately, this decision has accomplished the opposite.

title: Warning - Safety / Fire Issue  - Hopper Fire
text:
Hours after we shut down our Traeger Woodridge Pro pellet grill and believed it had completely cooled, we began smelling smoke. To our surprise, the pellets in the hopper had ignited. We immediately opened the pellet-release door and emptied the burning/smoldering pellets into a pail of water.

What concerns me most is that this happened hours after the grill had been turned off. Had our windows not been open and we hadn't noticed the smell of smoke, I don't know how far this could have progressed. It appears that pellets can ignite or smolder in the auger and potentially spread back into the hopper, which is extremely concerning.

The following morning, I attempted to turn the grill on. The power switch lights up, but the digital display remains completely dark and the grill is nonfunctional. Given what happened, I am concerned that internal components or electronics may have been damaged.

I contacted Traeger and requested either a replacement grill or an authorized service technician to inspect it. I was told that neither a complete replacement nor an in-home service visit was an option. Instead, the proposed solution was to send me replacement parts that I would be expected to install myself—including potentially replacing electronics, controls, or other internal components.

This is where I have a serious problem with the warranty experience. After an incident involving smoke and burning pellets inside the hopper, I don't believe a customer should be expected to diagnose the cause and start replacing electrical and control components. In my opinion, a qualified technician should determine why the hopper incident occurred in the first place before the grill is put back into service.

I spent approximately $800 on this Woodridge Pro less than a year ago, so this is extremely disappointing. My biggest concern isn't simply that the grill stopped working; it's that I no longer have confidence in its safety. Replacing parts may get the grill operating again, but it doesn't necessarily explain why pellets were burning in the hopper hours after shutdown.

I'm replacing this grill with a Weber propane grill because, after this experience, I'm simply not comfortable continuing to use it.

Does this incident indicate an inherent problem with the product? I can't make that determination. I can only describe what happened with my grill. Based on my experience, however, I no longer have confidence in the safety of this product and am out the 800 dollars I spent.

  Maintaining temp much easier than the green egg!

title: Broken out of the box
text: Came out of the box with a cut cord. Now I’ve got to wait an extra week for the part to come in for me to fix the grill I just bought.

title: Fantastic and reliable
text: Excellent grill has served me well for over 5 years without any issues,  easy to clean, just get the bamboo cutting board to wet or it will delaminate.  It holds the heat very well and does great low and slow pork butt.

title: After a Year of Living with It
text:
I've lived with this cooker for over a year now, (2 summers) and I think 4 stars is a very fair review for it. First of all, it feels high-quality, the interface is easier to use and the app is elite! Plenty of cooking space and the cooker hold temps precisely. I've even smoked in about 20 degree weather on a couple of times and this cooker  holds temps without any help from thermal blankets or any other tricks or accessories. I've very happy with the quality overall, and the general experience with this smoker. 

The Cons: This thing chews through pellets like crazy. Doesn't matter if you use theirs, or other high-quality pellets. I just smoked a Pork butt for 10 hours yesterday and used 3/4 of a bag of Treager pellets. Which are not cheap mind you. So yeah, it holds temps well, but it will eat away at your hopper. For what it's worth, I ONLY use this to smoke and the temp rarely ever exceeds 275 on it. I can only image how fast it eats up pellets if you try using this as a grill. 

The other con, which is actually just really annoying.. is because of the position of the hopper measurement laser letting you know how full of pellets it is, is directly over the hole where the pellets get fed into the firebox... It's contantly yelling at me that my hopper is low on pellets. Meanwhile, a mountain of them are still in there, it's just that the laser is pointing at the lowest possible part of the hopper. So I go outside, slide the pellets down and even them out and it's fine. But it's really annoying to deal with. You never actually know how many pellets are in the hopper because you can't trust this measurement. I have on occasion, ignored the notice that my hopper is low because of this problem realizing eventually the mountain of pellets would tumble down on their own, just to realize it actually is low and I need to put more pellets in. I with you could move the little measuring laser to a different spot in the hopper. 

One more thing not necessarily about this cooker, that is common but I wish someone would fix. I bought the accessory tray that snaps onto the front so that I have a little bit of space when putting stuff on/off the cooker. However, the handle to open the lid sticks out pretty far. So like... 25% of the space I gained from buying this tray, is gone because the handle is blocking it. I wish someone would figure out putting that type of accessory on one of the sides so it sticks out like an "L" shape. Prep on the shelf, and then 90 degree turn right onto the cooker.

title: Waste of money
text: Bought the grill June of 2026 have called 5 times with issues of a non functioning non working grill. Their solution is to ship parts that “may” fix the issue the catch is you have to install them without directions and when the part can’t even be replaced with the help of customer service they send you another part. Waste of time money food and pellets. Buyer beware do not waste YOUR money on a this grill or on a company that doesn’t stand behind their faulty products!!!!

title: Caught on fire and almost burned my house down!
text: This grill worked for about a year then stopped heating up or would shoot fire out of the control box. I called and spoke with customer service several times. They replaced several parts which I had to hire a handyman to install. Then after working on and off for a few months it caught on fire and burned so badly the grill itself was bubbling and melting. there was no food in it. I was just trying to heat it up. Now I have no grill and customer service would not do anything about it even with video and pics.

title: Works good...with a little extra work
text: The only issue I have with my Ironwood XL is a temp difference of 30-40 degrees hotter on the left side of the grill vs the right side. The right side actually runs a little cool and the left side runs 20 to 30 degrees hot. Having bbq'ed for 40 years this isn't a deal breaker, but by the advertising I looked at before buying, I expected this to be the evenest cooking surface temp. out there. Also $200 for a cover, $200 for a front shelf, and $300 to $400 more for PAL accessories, not including the storage bins for pellets, the final price was close to $3000. So 4 stars instead of 5. Build quality is good...not great related to the price. Some other premium grills in this price range are built was thicker steel and more robust but would cost $500 to $1000 more. I've owned my Traeger for 4 months now and have had very good results with brisket, pork butts, ribs, poppers, pizza, meat loaf, ect, etc, etc. I really do enjoy using it and am getting better and better at running this pit the more I use it. Overall I'm pretty happy so far, but satisfaction will be based on longevity along with the performance, so we will see. I would expect this grill to last 15 years minimum. Anything short of that will not be acceptable.

title: Great grill until you need tech support.
text: The lid on my 18 month old Timberline 1300 grill almost fell off during a grill session.  The left side shoulder bolt broke and fell out.  I called tech support and after about 30 minutes on the call, I was told they would ship me a replace bolt assembly.  Well, when it arrived, it looked like a completely different part.  I called back to tech support and finally got to a supervisor named Nour for assistance.  He asked me to disassemble the inside heat shield to gain access to install a washer and lock-nut only to find out the inside not was tack-welded during and would not accept the new parts that arrived.  The grill worked great for the first 18 months and now....not so much.  Shame on your technical staff folks for not getting the job done properly or timely.
